title: HB 5221 (2011-2012 Regular Session, Michigan Legislature (bill page title: "House Bill 5221 of 2011")): Elections; registration; proof of United States citizenship when registering to vote; require. Amends sec. 509q of 1954 PA 116 (MCL 168.509q ) & adds sec. 496a.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) (b) A legible photocopy of the applicant's birth certificate that verifies United States citizenship to the satisfaction of the person processing the voter registration application.
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) (d) A legible photocopy of the pertinent pages of the applicant's United States passport identifying the applicant and the applicant's passport number.
(b_no_id_remedy) not stated.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship)
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) (1) Voter registration applications shall contain a statement requiring an applicant to submit satisfactory evidence of United States citizenship with his or her application and stating that the application shall be rejected if satisfactory evidence of United States citizenship is not provided.
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) (2) A person processing voter registration applications at a department of state office, a designated voter registration agency, or a county, city, township, or village clerk's office shall reject a voter registration application that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of United States citizenship.
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) Satisfactory evidence of United States citizenship includes any of the following:
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) (a) The applicant's driver license number or personal identification card number issued by the department of state or the equivalent department of another state if that department indicates on the applicant's driver license or personal identification card that the person has provided satisfactory evidence of United States citizenship.
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) (f) Other documents or methods of proof that are used to establish United States citizenship pursuant to the immigration reform and control act of 1986, Public Law 99-603, 100 Stat. 3359.
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) (3) For purposes of this section, proof of voter registration from another state is not satisfactory evidence of United States citizenship.
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) (4) Notwithstanding subsection (2), a person who is registered to vote in this state on the effective date of the amendatory act that added this section shall not be required to submit evidence of United States citizenship unless the person moves his or her residence to another city, township, or village.
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) (5) After a person submits satisfactory evidence of citizenship, the city, township, or village clerk shall add this information to the qualified voter file.
(section) Sec. 496a (as in the version read)
(quote) The city, township, or village clerk may destroy all documents submitted as evidence of United States citizenship not less than 2 years after the date of submission.
(e_other_rule) not stated.
(other) Sec. 509q: begins "The qualified voter file shall contain all of the following information for each qualified voter:"
